notes.bundled source (T6 S3): This file is the plugin-bundled adapter source: exactly one duo-adapter.json at the root of the plugin's own directory, scanned only while the plugin is ACTIVE (docs/guides/adapter-authoring.md, 'Adapters a plugin bundles'). The file name is a constant and therefore carries no identity, so `name` is the identity and `plugin` MUST name the exact plugin basename that bundles it — the file, not the directory. `version_range` is mandatory for the same reason: `plugin` is declared, and a declared plugin without a bounded range is refused at load as unbounded support.
notes.options (verified against acme-catalog.p: The namespace claim ^acme_catalog_ takes OWNERSHIP of both option names this plugin writes, and both are classified here, so nothing in the namespace falls through to the pending queue. acme_catalog_settings is written once at activation and thereafter only by an operator (authored). acme_catalog_cache is bumped by the template_redirect hook on every front-end request and by nothing else (runtime): it is target-local traffic state, never branchable, and the walk asserts it does not reach captured state.
notes.post_types/taxonomies: acme_item and acme_kind are both `authored`. A manifest cannot declare post-type SCOPE — that list is site-local policy — but `duo init` seeds policy.post_types/policy.taxonomies from every authored declaration in the manifests it selects (agent/src/Init/InitPlanner.php), which is how these two reach scope without a hand edit.
notes.option_autoload preserve: An authored option must declare an autoload disposition or the manifest is refused at load: insertion may never guess (agent/src/Policy/ManifestGrammar.php). `preserve` is the honest answer for this plugin — it calls add_option() with core's default and never sets autoload itself, so Duo carries the target's existing value across rather than asserting one.
notes.tables deliberately undeclared: acme_catalog_index is created by this plugin's activation hook and is intentionally absent from this manifest. It is the walk's undeclared-table subject: coverage finds it, assess mints its `table:acme_catalog_index` row, and the release's database checkpoint is the only thing that restores it. Declaring it `runtime` here would remove exactly the finding S3 exists to observe.
